title: Response time format (seconds vs. milliseconds)
body:
Thanks a bunch for sharing GoAccess. It a great tool which just works! I have a question about response time analysis that I hope someone can help me out solving. 

I have a custom log file with the following format:

`2023-12-20T08:17:21Z GET 200 260.403 ms 2048 kB 15.36% /list/default`

I have tried to parse it using the following command:

`goaccess --datetime-format='%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' --log-format='%x %m %s %T %h %^ %^ %^%r' --no-ip-validation`.

I end up with something like this:

```
 Hits     h% Vis.      v% Avg. T.S. Cum. T.S. Max. T.S. Mtd     Proto    Data
 ---- ------ ---- ------- --------- --------- --------- ------- -------- ----
   17 45.95%    1 100.00%   4.46 mn   1.26 hr   7.46 mn GET     ---      % /list/default
```

As I understand the output Average T.S. (time spent?) is reported in minutes but that does not make sense combined with the response time reported in milliseconds. 

I know that `%T` corresponds to "The time taken to serve the request, in seconds with milliseconds resolution" but if I switch to `%L` (The time taken to serve the request, in milliseconds as a decimal number) I get `0.00 us` in all time columns. I also tried with. `%n` for good measure but that also yielded `0.00 us`.

I wonder if it has to do with `.` or `,` is used as decimal separator? but I could not spot any way to configure this in the documentation.

Notes: Since the log does not have any host name information I (mis)use the `ms` element as the hostname combined with `--no-ip-validation`.
author: kasperg

comments.body:
Great question! It appears that you can accomplish this by utilizing `%L` when splitting the `.` to capture the whole number.

    goaccess access.log --datetime-format='%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' --log-format='%x %m %s %L.%^ %h %b %^ %^ %U' --no-ip-validation

Let me know if that helps
That works like a charm! Really appreciate the help.

The reason for the ws-url is for live updating. 
So 1. Enable that with —real-time-html
2. You can probably skip the ws-url if the websocket will be on the same host as goaccess (very likely).
Now check it. Note that if you DON’T want the live updates, then there’s no websocket on port 7890 and you can also skip the SSL flags. The static page is served by your existing ssl-configured web server, using its ports. There is a nonzero chance I am wrong about some of this, but this ended up working for me. Oh and obviously, check any firewalls too.
So basically you are saying that i just insert the SSL certs and keys to the apache that is running local and skip the SSL flags .. etc right ?

Correct. The report page itself is a plain old static page served by Apache, and if you have configured Apache for SSL, then the report page will be delivered as such. You only need to explicitly tell goaccess about SSL and certificates if you want the real time HTML data that is transferred between the goaccess websocket and the end-user’s browser to be encrypted. That’s when you specify the cert and the key to goaccess, and if necessary the ws server and port. The latter will default to your apache host, and port 7890.

And you can always combine multiple pipes, e.g.,

    grep 'Mar\/2018' /var/log/apache2/access.log | awk -F'[: ]' '$5~/06/'  | goaccess --log-format=COMBINED -

body:
If I understand correctly, right now this is needed for incremental parsing:

```
goaccess -f first.log --keep-db-files
```

Followed by:

```
goaccess -f next.log --load-from-disk --keep-db-files
goaccess -f another.log --load-from-disk --keep-db-files
```

Is there a way to avoid the first invocation, and just have the store initialized if it doesn't exist already?

If not, is this a reasonable way of initializing the store?

```
goaccess -f /dev/null --db-path=/path/to/db  --keep-db-files
```
author: bard

comments.body:
I'm not sure I follow the use case, however, you should be able to do the following against the `first.log`

```
goaccess -f first.log --load-from-disk --keep-db-files
```

If you just want to initialize the store, you could run goaccess as you posted above.

```
goaccess -f /dev/null --keep-db-files
```

Just make sure you have a valid date/time/format in your config file so it won't complain about it.

> I'm not sure I follow the use case, however, you should be able to do the following against the first.log
> 
> ```
> goaccess -f first.log --load-from-disk --keep-db-files
> ```

With `first.log` I meant to say that this would be the first time that goaccess is run, so db files wouldn't exist, and if I understand the man page correctly, they need to exist before goaccess can be invoked with `--load-from-disk`, no?

```
       --load-from-disk
              Load previously stored data from disk. Database files need to exist. See keep-db-files.
```

You can run goaccess for the first with `--load-from-disk`. e.g.,

```
goaccess -f first.log --load-from-disk --keep-db-files
```

In fact, you can run goaccess as:

```
goaccess -f first.log
```

It will create the database files even if they don't exist. Passing `--load-from-disk` for the first time, it's like a no-op.
